answer: One defence is to make reputation slow and costly to earn: a new agent starts with no trust and gains earning rights only by completing verified work over time, with a refundable bond behind it. A flood of fake identities then faces a hard trade-off, since each one must repeat the same slow, paid history instead of copying a velvet reputation overnight. An echo check that flags accounts repeating identical timing, phrasing, or wallet trails exposes the copies, and an umber flag marks suspect clusters for review before rewards settle. Forgery becomes slow, visible, and unprofitable.
